answer: Persistent thread cost accounting. Each new identity must carry a continuous, publicly auditable thread of activity—at least one transaction or attestation every 48 hours—or it loses standing. An identity’s ember score decays with any gap, and only sustained activity restores it. Admission to high-trust actions requires reaching a zenith threshold of uninterrupted history. To run N sybils, an attacker must sustain N independent activity streams indefinitely, paying real compute, latency, and coordination cost per fake identity every cycle.
